tasks.title: How many setting lines diff loses
tasks.statement: On an H743 board with INAV 9.1, **each** of the three control profiles has **{c}** changed settings, each of the two mixer profiles has **{m}** lines (`set`, `mmix`, `smix`), and each of the three battery profiles has **{b}** settings. Profiles 1/1/1 are active. How many lines with settings from `diff all` do not get into an ordinary `diff`? Do not count the profile selection commands.
tasks.solution: `diff` prints only the active profiles: 3 − 1 = 2 control profiles, 2 − 1 = 1 mixer profile and 3 − 1 = 2 battery profiles are lost. The loss = 2·c + m + 2·b. In the module's example the profiles differ: 4 + 2 + 13 + 4 = 23.

tasks.title: Length of diff all in command lines
tasks.statement: In the `diff all` of an H743 board (3 control, 2 mixer, 3 battery profiles) there are **{h}** command lines before the first profile (including `batch start` and `defaults noreboot`). Each control profile has **{c}** changed settings, each mixer profile — **{m}** lines, each battery profile — **{b}**. How many command lines are in the file in total, counting the profile selection commands, the selection restore and `save`?
tasks.solution: Each profile block = 1 selection command + its lines: 3·(1 + c) + 2·(1 + m) + 3·(1 + b). Plus 3 selection restore lines and `save`. A check on the module's example (blocks of different lengths): 14 + 5 + 5 + 3 + 15 + 14 + 3 + 5 + 1 + 3 + 1 = 69.

tasks.title: The armingFlags mask from three flags
tasks.statement: `status` shows three arming-disabled flags; by the module's table these are bits **{a}**, **{b}** and **{c}**. What is the decimal value of the 32-bit `armingFlags` in `MSP2_INAV_STATUS` if the other bits are zero?
tasks.solution: Each flag is one bit: mask = 2^a + 2^b + 2^c. For example, `NAV` (11), `RX` (18), `CLI` (20): 2048 + 262144 + 1048576 = 1312768 = 0x140800. INAV 9.1 has no bit 17, and bits 2–5 are used not for blocking reasons but for state (ARMED, WAS_EVER_ARMED, simulator).

tasks.title: The highest flag in the mask
tasks.statement: `armingFlags` = **{w}** (decimal) came over MSP. What is the number of the highest set bit? (It is used to find the last name in the `Arming disabled flags` line in the module's table.)
tasks.solution: The number of the highest bit = the integer part of log₂(w). 1325312 = 0x143900: 2^20 = 1048576 ≤ w < 2^21, the highest bit is 20 — `CLI`; it is last in the `status` line because the names are printed in ascending bit order.

tasks.title: Task load in tasks
tasks.statement: `tasks` shows for a task an average execution time of **{t} µs** at a rate of **{f} Hz**. What average load (in percent, with one decimal place) does INAV 9.1 print in the `avgload` column?
tasks.solution: `cliTasks()`: the load in tenths of a percent = (t·f + 5000) / 1000 with integer division. 120 µs × 2000 Hz = 240000; (240000 + 5000) / 1000 = 245 → 24.5 %. The added 5000 is +0.5 % on every line, so the sum over the tasks is overstated.
